title: FLA import: CPicVideoStream (docs/21 sec 18.2) has no decoder — embedded-video placements hit the unknown-class skip path; readCPicVideo layout is inferred and contradicts the spec
description: deserializeClass (flash8-binary.ts:1208-1254) dispatches CPicVideo only; there is NO case for CPicVideoStream, the class docs/21 sec 18.2 lays out in full (InstanceHeader, u32 frameLeft/Right/Top/Bottom crop rect, u8 0, BomString empty, BomString name, u32 1, u16 videoId) and whose confidence sec 20 lists as Verified. A real Flash 8 FLA with a placed video object would therefore fall into the unknown-class warn+skip path (boundary re-sync), losing the placement. Meanwhile readCPicVideo (:2435-2449) implements an admittedly INFERRED layout (schema byte + matrix + u16 mediaId, comment: 'no fixture FLA with video was available to verify') that matches neither sec 18.2's field list nor any fixture. Task 0877 (done) added CPicVideo handling but never covered CPicVideoStream. STATUS: unconfirmed / needs a real-FLA fixture with embedded video — no repo fixture contains either class, so both the missing dispatch and the inferred layout are unproven. Why it matters: video import silently degrades on real files, and one of docs-vs-code must be wrong (see also the docs-accuracy task 1407 which flags the sec 20 'Verified' claim). Fix: obtain/author a Flash 8 fixture with an embedded video placed on stage (real Flash 8 oracle needed); then implement readCPicVideoStream per the verified bytes, wire it in deserializeClass, map its crop rect + name onto VideoDisplayObject, and correct readCPicVideo or the doc as the fixture dictates. Acceptance: fixture-driven import test asserting the video placement (position, crop, mediaId->library link) plus round-trip through the writer if/when video write support exists; until a fixture exists, at minimum add the CPicVideoStream dispatch with a conservative boundary-resync body and a targeted warning naming the class.
